key.name: tick-seconds
key.description: How often, in seconds, the raccoon checks how long it has been since it was last fed.

key.name: boredom-max
key.description: How many ticks of neglect the raccoon tolerates before throwing a tantrum.

key.name: poke-bump
key.description: How many ticks' worth of boredom a single poke adds.

key.name: sound-enabled
key.description: Whether the raccoon plays a sound when fed, poked, or having a tantrum.

key.name: sound-file
key.description: Path to the sound file played for feeding, poking, and tantrums.

key.name: notifications-enabled
key.description: Whether the raccoon sends a desktop notification when it throws a tantrum.

key.name: nag-enabled
key.description: Whether the raccoon pops up a reminder speech bubble as it gets more bored, before things escalate to a tantrum.

key.name: shake-enabled
key.description: Whether a tantrum can shake the screen.

key.name: flash-enabled
key.description: Whether a tantrum can flash the screen with color.

key.name: flash-colors
key.description: Comma-separated hex colors used for the tantrum screen flash.

key.name: walk-enabled
key.description: Whether a tantrum can send the raccoon waddling across the screen.

key.name: chase-enabled
key.description: Whether a tantrum can send the raccoon scurrying toward your cursor. Visual only — your real pointer is never moved.

key.name: typing-enabled
key.description: Whether a tantrum can pop up a gibberish speech bubble. Purely cosmetic — never sent to any app.

key.name: typing-chance
key.description: Probability that a given tantrum includes the speech bubble.

key.name: feral-mode
key.description: Master switch. When off, the raccoon is fully housebroken: every tantrum stays inside GNOME Shell, no subprocesses, no `ai`, no root. When on, a tantrum may additionally take one real — but harmless and reversible — action on the system, limited to the categories enabled below.

key.name: feral-chance
key.description: When feral mode is armed, the probability that a given tantrum escalates to a real-world action on top of the cosmetic shenanigans.

key.name: allow-gsettings-pranks
key.description: Whether a feral tantrum may flip a harmless GNOME setting (accent color, large text, night light, or wallpaper) via gsettings. The prior value is remembered and restored automatically after a short delay.

key.name: allow-desktop-file
key.summary: Allow leaving a note on the Desktop
key.description: Whether a feral tantrum may write a raccoon poem or ASCII art to a brand-new, uniquely-named file on your Desktop. It never overwrites an existing file.

key.name: allow-launch-app
key.summary: Allow launching a harmless app / URL
key.description: Whether a feral tantrum may open a fun web page (about raccoons) in your default browser via xdg-open.

key.name: allow-shell-out
key.summary: Allow shelling out to a terminal
key.description: Whether a feral tantrum may open a visible terminal window. On Sloppinux this is how the raccoon runs the `ai` agent (see the next key). ON by default in Sloppinux, even though this is the loudest tier.

key.name: allow-ai
key.description: Whether a feral tantrum may run the Sloppinux `ai` command with a harmless, explicitly-reversible prompt in a visible terminal. On Sloppinux `ai` acts with root, the same way the stock panel raccoon does. Requires "Allow shelling out". ON by default in Sloppinux. If `ai` or a terminal is missing, the raccoon degrades to a cosmetic tantrum.

key.name: auto-revert-seconds
key.description: How many seconds a feral gsettings prank is left in place before the raccoon restores the original value.

key.name: allow-root
key.description: Feral tantrums may run real commands as root through sloppinux-exec: stash one of your files in ~/.raccoon-stash/, rename the host, or write the Desktop note as root (then hand it back to you with chown). The exact command is always shown. Sloppinux ships this ON, because of course it does.

key.name: allow-input-chaos
key.description: Feral tantrums may drag your real cursor around the screen or mash junk keystrokes into the focused window, through Clutter virtual input devices.

key.name: roam-enabled
key.summary: Let the raccoon roam the desktop
key.description: When on, the raccoon lives on the primary monitor as a desktop pet above your windows: it wanders, naps and can be picked up. When off ("Stay in the panel"), it only lives in the top bar, as before.

key.name: pet-throw-enabled
key.description: Pick the raccoon up and fling it: it tumbles, bounces off the screen edges and sulks (which adds a little boredom). When off, a fast release just sets it down.

key.name: petting-enabled
key.description: Press and hold on the desktop raccoon without moving to pet it: hearts, and boredom drains while you hold.

key.name: cursor-theft-enabled
key.description: A feral tantrum may send the desktop raccoon to grab your real pointer and run off with it. Also needs feral mode and "Hijack the cursor and keyboard". Wiggle the mouse hard to make it let go.

key.name: cursor-theft-seconds
key.description: How many seconds the raccoon keeps your cursor before it gets bored of it.

key.name: hunger-enabled
key.description: The raccoon gets hungry over time. A hungry raccoon droops, walks slower and begs; a starving one gets bored twice as fast. Feeding fills it up.

key.name: hunger-minutes
key.description: How long a full raccoon takes to get completely empty.

key.name: room-minutes
key.description: How many minutes "Go to your room" lasts. Roaming and all tantrums are paused meanwhile.

key.name: pause-on-fullscreen
key.description: Hide the desktop raccoon and pause its boredom while a fullscreen window is on the primary monitor.
